target_claim: The reduction (three copies per vertex, copy-copy edges for i!=j, same-index edges for H-edges, k=m+1) maps 3-colorable graphs H to feasible river-crossing instances (Claim 1 iff). In fact the constructed instance is never feasible: the three copies of each vertex form a triangle, so a valid first trip needs at least 2 copies of every vertex in S (|S|>=2m), but |S|<=k-1=m. The claimed step-1 crossing 'C2 union C3 is independent' is false since v(2),v(3) are enemies.
source_quote:
Claim 1. H is 3-colorable if and only if there exists a valid crossing sequence for the con-
structed instance.
test_sketch: Implement the construction verbatim (lines 0029-0035): for H with vertices VH and edges EH, build G on {v(i)} with edges {(u(i),v(i)):(u,v) in EH} plus {(v(i),v(j)): i!=j}, k=m+1. Brute-force oracle: BFS over states (L,R,c) with the validity/transition rules of lines 0015-0026 (state space small: n=3m<=12 for m<=4). Input family: H = K1 (m=1) and H = K2 (m=2), both trivially 3-colorable. Constructed instance for K1 is a triangle {v(1),v(2),v(3)} with k=2; BFS shows the goal state is unreachable (any first trip of <=1 passenger leaves two mutually-hostile copies on the left without Charon), refuting the forward direction of Claim 1. Same failure for K2 and every m>=1.
